metadata.title: Level Set Method; partial regularity in ${\mathbf R}^3$
metadata.abstract: In the level set method, all level sets of a function move by mean curvature. The function is then a solution of a degenerate parabolic equation, the level set equation. Since the beginning of the 1990s it has been known that solutions are Lipschitz and, in general, not $C^2$. We show that, along a level set that is initially a smooth closed surface in ${\mathbf R}^3$, the Hessian of the solution is bounded up to its first singular time. In fact, at each non-generic singularity the Hessian tends to zero, at a rate given by its instability. Using these bounds, we show in the sequel that, surprisingly, at the singular time the solution is twice differentiable and has a backward time derivative at every point of the level set, whatever the singularity, and identify both the Hessian and time derivative.
